source_document.body:
It’s that time of year again; Black Friday approaches! And while the e-bike sales have been pretty good all month, there’s no better day than today to find an amazing deal on a new way around your city (or a fitness e-bike, leisure e-bike, cargo e-bike, etc…)!
A lot of sites will throw a lot of affiliate links at you today for anything they can hawk for a few bucks (this site included from our deals team, probably). But this isn’t that. I’m a professional e-bike rider and tester, and the deals below are only for bikes I actually ride, and for companies I would actually recommend to my own family and friends. Basically, this is the good stuff.
Lectric eBikes
Let’s start with Lectric eBikes, since, as the largest e-bike company in North America, they have long been setting the standard for incredible deals and value in the e-bike industry. I’ve long said that you can’t get better value than here. Sure, you can find lower-priced e-bikes out there, but not at this quality level and with this level of customer support.
Lectric’s sales are usually defined by huge collections of free accessories added to their already low-priced e-bikes, further increasing the value. But this year there are also some legit price drops as well. See all of their Black Friday Sales packages here.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
The major standouts for me have always been the XP and XP Lite lines.
The latest of each, the XP4 and the XP Lite3 , offer bundle deals with savings of up to $731 and $257 , respectively. For price drops, you’ll find that both the Lectrix XPLite 2 and the XPTrike2 are marked down to new record-low prices.
I’m also a huge fan of their cargo bike, the Lectric XPedition2 , which has savings of up to $405 thanks to those impressive bundles.
But you should also explore the rest of their deals because just about everything is either marked down or comes with a crazy amount of free accessories that you can’t get for this price any other time of the year!
Ride1Up
Ride1Up is another major value leader in the space, and in fact, I’ve been using the Ride1Up Roadster V3 as my everyday commuter e-bike since the summer.
I’m set to surpass 1,000 miles on it (1,600 km) by the end of the month!
That bike is marked down $100 to just $1,295 right now, making it a major deal for a lightweight, 40 lb (18 kg) commuter e-bike that doubles as a gravel bike. Ask me how I know that it can handle hard off-roading, too!
You can also save $150 on the Vorsa , which is an awesome all-around e-bike with multiple levels for riders who want higher or lower performance.
The new Portola 02 folder is a killer deal at $100 off for just $795 (that’s a crazy price!). If you want to go big and powerful, the Revv1 will crush Super73 and is doing so for $500 off !
Last but not least, the Prodigy V2 Eco is just $1,295 after the $100 deal, which is literally the most affordable Bosch-powered electric bike in the world. The only thing stopping me from buying that bike is that I already have one, though at this price, part of me wonders if I should get a spare for friends to use!
Basically, Ride1Up has a ton of Black Friday Sales going on now, and you can check them all out here .
Monarc Bikes
If you want to go a bit further up the quality ladder to get a more premium e-bike, but you still don’t want to spend $2k+, then you should check out Monarc Bikes . It was founded by Lectric eBikes as an offshoot that could focus on building higher-end models while still leveraging Lectric’s industry heavyweight status to get better pricing. That means the company can offer higher-end e-bikes that rival some of the bike shop brands, while still offering direct-to-consumer pricing, 5-year warranties, and industry-leading local customer support by phone and email.
The two models they’ve launched so far are the urban-focused Tracer and the off-road-optimized Marker, though you better believe they’ve got more interesting stuff coming, likely next year. For now, though, these two models cover most folks’ needs and come with higher-end parts like quad-piston hydraulic disc brakes, reverse arch forks, Bafang’s powerful motors, large batteries, and impressive add-ons like rear-facing radar to keep tabs on approaching cars.
The company started by selling e-bikes that came with a free spare battery, but has recently opened up options for single or even no-battery bikes, meaning if you previously bought a Monarc model and already have that free spare battery, you can save a bunch of money by buying only the bike and using your spare battery across the line. Yep, it’s like the power drill model!
You can see all of the sales and deals here!
JackRabbit
JackRabbit may be a bit of a divisive brand due to how different the bikes look, but I freakin’ love these things! My JackRabbit OG is one of my prized possessions, and I just love how much performance and convenience JackRabbit has been able to pack into small-format two-wheelers that start at barely 25 lb (11 kg).
Literally every one of their micro e-bikes is 20% off, meaning you’re saving hundreds of dollars. But then the rest of their gear is up to 50% off, such as 30% off their big RangeBuster batteries.
Check out all of the sales here .
The awesomeness of JackRabbit’s Micro-bikes is a micro-hill I’m prepared to die on, and I definitely recommend these models to anyone who wants a compact electric two-wheeler that rides as stable as a typical Class 2 e-bike but can fold flat to fit in a tiny space like behind a couch or under a dorm room bed.
I’m never parting with my own JackRabbit, and I love seeing new riders discover just how much fun these awesomely strange bikes are!
Mod Bikes
Austin, Texas-based Mod Bikes doesn’t get as much press as some of the larger players, but I think they deserve a second look for several reasons. Not only are they continuously pushing out new and impressive bikes as well as cool technology alongside them (don’t forget about their locking streetside charging stands for e-bikes! ), but they also have cool rides that no one else has managed to create.
Case in point: The Mod Easy Sidecar e-bike that looks like a million bucks, but costs just $3,495 after the $400 deal for Black Friday. I love this e-bike for riding around with my nephews as well as the family dog, which you can see below.
There’s even a Sahara version of it that looks like it just got back from an incredible desert expedition!
Juiced Bikes
Juiced Bikes was revived this year , and the company is back with a vengeance! The high-performance bikes are better than ever, and the prices are bette r, too!
The recently launched Scrambler Mini leads the pack in pricing, starting at just $949 thanks to its Black Friday promotional price. That’d be an awesome model for any young riders this season. But the larger versions are also pushing the value war forward with their own great sales.
There’s a lot to like here, from higher-end parts to 5-year warranties to the backing of the nation’s largest e-bike company, Lectric eBikes. Basically, it’s hard to imagine finding a better deal on a moto-style electric bike these days than from Juiced.
VMAX electric scooters
Sure, e-bikes are my first love, but electric scooters absolutely deserve their place in the micromobility ecosystem thanks to their extreme portability and compact, space-saving size.
VMAX is my favorite electric scooter company, which brings its Swiss design to the US and European scooter markets. When it came to putting my nephew on a scooter to get to school, I made sure he had a VMAX VX2 Lite to cruise around safely and securely. That scooter is marked down to just $639 for Black Friday, despite offering impressive performance of 25 mph (40 km/h) and over 50 miles (80 km) of range! I reviewed that scooter recently and can tell you that the price is more than worth it!
The new VX4 is a 37 mph (60 km/h) model that is on sale for just $1,199, though you can get the previous version of that scooter with slightly more muted performance for an even better price of $889!
There are a lot of great deals to be had, and you can see all of VMAX’s sales here .
Any more I should add?
These are the major sales that jumped out at me, but let me know what other sales you’ve seen on e-bikes you recommend.
I’ll take a look too and update if I see something I know I can stand behind. There are a lot of great e-bikes out there, and having ridden so many by now, I love being able to share my experiences, especially when there’s a good deal to be had at the end!
